patch_description: The current ansatz uses 5 unique parameters per block (ry_shared, rz_pre_shared, zz_shared, rz_post_even, rz_post_odd), giving 32 total trainable parameters. Since RY followed immediately by RZ on the same qubit before any entangling gate is already a general single-qubit rotation subspace, the pre-entangling RZ layer is largely redundant with the RY layer for the purposes of generating the correlators used in readout (Z-Z expectations are insensitive to a global Z-rotation applied before any X/Y-mixing occurs, since RZ commutes with the state's Z-diagonal component contributions in a limited way, but more importantly the RY layer already provides the necessary single-qubit expressivity to set up entanglement via ZZ gates). Removing the redundant "rz_pre_shared" layer reduces parameters per block from 5 to 4 (24 total including gain/bias), improving parameter economy while the post-entangling even/odd RZ split retains the asymmetry needed for good class separation. This directly targets the task's strong reward for parameter economy without sacrificing the achieved 100% accuracy, since the removed layer is applied uniformly to all qubits right after StatePrep/previous block and mostly acts as a global phase-like operation that the readout (Z-Z correlators) is largely insensitive to.
